summary: This case study analyzes 1,808 provider submission attempts across 58 production projects on the Genflick Film Studio platform during a two-week window. The authors empirically demonstrate that LLM calls dominate API activity (72.1%) in multi-stage generative video systems and illustrate how unfinished project pipelines skew naive workload averages. The work provides immediate practical value for architecture and capacity planning, backed by an embedded 58-row dataset and arithmetic verification script.
strengths: High practical relevance for AI system architects and operators building multimodal generation pipelines, clearly illustrating request distribution and workload bottlenecks.

Exemplary transparency and methodological honesty regarding unfinished-work bias, distinguishing observed attempts from wire-level HTTP counts, and separating creator traffic from internal QA/admin usage.
Fully reproducible descriptive statistics enabled by the inclusion of the complete 58-row anonymized CSV extract and standard-library Python validation script directly within the text.
Nuanced treatment of denominators, demonstrating why authored durations or clip targets cannot be naively equated to API request volume or final export outputs.
weaknesses: The primary supporting artifact repository is private, precluding independent inspection of raw operational traces or wire captures.
The sample of creator projects reaching actual video generation within the study window is very small (n=2), which limits broader statistical inferences regarding completed film production costs.
Request volumes are not correlated with token/byte counts, latency, or dollar expenditures, which restricts financial forecasting.
suggestions: Incorporate token counts and latency distributions alongside raw request counts in future studies to evaluate whether LLM request predominance translates into cost or latency dominance.
Track an entry cohort over an extended longitudinal window until export completion to establish a statistically grounded profile of completed film generations.
Provide a sanitized open-source repository for the verification harness and descriptive analysis scripts rather than relying entirely on inline text extracts.

claims.text: In this sample, 72.1% of recorded provider submission attempts were LLM work.
claims.source: Verified via arithmetic reproduction from the provided 58-project production CSV: 1,304 LLM attempts out of 1,808 total attempts equals 72.12%.

claims.text: The 21 creator projects created within the window recorded 591 attempts, for a mean of 28.142857, median 13, and P90 47.
claims.source: Verified via execution of the dataset and quantile calculations: the 21 rows matching account='creator' and new=1 sum to 591 (mean 28.143), with a median of 13 and linear interpolation 90th percentile of 47.0.

claims.text: Genflick combines AI film planning, storyboards, video generation, and clip editing with separate workflows for episodic series and music videos.
